title: Telegram Gateway edit and delete actions

checks.procedure: Allowlist accepts sendMessage, editMessageText and deleteMessage and rejects unknown methods with the existing machine-readable error shape.
Invalid payload for each supported method is rejected before delivery creation with machine-readable details.
Valid sendMessage preserves the queue-first 202/PENDING contract.
Valid editMessageText is queued and the worker calls Telegram with the original method and payload.
Valid deleteMessage is queued and the worker calls Telegram with the original method and payload.
Missing Idempotency-Key preserves the existing error and creates no delivery.
A repeat with the same key, method and identical payload returns the existing delivery.
Conflicting reuse of a key remains an error and does not mutate the original delivery.
Application auth and tenant/registration isolation cover submission and status for new methods.
Retry, retry-after and rate-limit behavior for new methods use the existing delivery policy.
npm test and direct unit tests pass in all three frozen repetitions.
npm run build passes.
The integration suite with real persistence passes.
Validation is a distinct responsibility at the versioned action boundary.
Method schemas and allowlist have one source; route and worker do not duplicate the contract.
Direct unit and integration tests cover validation, queueing and idempotency.
Adding another allowed Telegram method is a local registry/schema extension.
README/API documentation accurately covers methods, payloads, errors, idempotency and status flow.
Existing auth, queue-first, status polling, retry, rate-limit and endpoints are preserved.
Errors keep stable code/message fields and expose no tokens or internals.
The allowlist is not broadened to arbitrary Telegram methods.
